finding.claim: Exactly one production-reachable authoritative F-17 publication path exists (worker PUBLISH over pipe -> Publisher.handle -> durable_publish -> build_anchor_record -> Anchor V2 record + committed watermark); every other anchor/watermark writer is test-only, recovery-only, a re-export shim, or an unwired probe harness.
evidence: THE ONE PATH, END TO END: provisioned Windows service entry is ONLY 'from gnosis.trust.publisher_service import main' (src/gnosis/provision/provisioner.py:334); run_service builds the single PipeServer wired to publisher.handle (src/gnosis/trust/publisher_service.py:155-159); PipeServer dispatches every request through exactly one handler call self.handler(request, client_pid) (src/gnosis/trust/pipe_server.py:251).

Publisher is the sole handler: exactly one class Publisher (src/gnosis/trust/publisher.py:108) and one def handle (publisher.py:122); the grammar accepts only 'PUBLISH <run_id>' (publisher.py:59); _handle calls durable_publish (publisher.py:201) and is the ONLY construction site of PublicationRequest (publisher.py:144).

durable_publish has exactly ONE caller in src/gnosis: publisher.py:201 (grep for 'durable_publish(' across src returns only its def at publication.py:706 and this call). Inside _publish_locked it is the single site that does all three authoritative writes: build_anchor_record (publication.py:774), store.append (publication.py:777), _commit_watermark (publication.py:813), then mark_anchored (publication.py:828).

AnchorStore.append (the low-level ledger writer, anchor.py:263) has exactly two callers: publish_anchor at anchor.py:525 and _publish_locked at publication.py:777. The many other '.append(' hits are Python list.append or the kernel run-event Ledger.append (signature append(run_id,event_type,data)), a different class, not the anchor ledger.

publish_anchor (Stage-3 writer, anchor.py:513; appends a record but writes NO watermark) is TEST-ONLY: its only call sites repo-wide are tests/test_authority_boundary.py (lines 171,182,194,212,228,239,424,436,446,463,499). No caller exists in src/gnosis, so it is not a second production path.

The watermark writer _commit_watermark (publication.py:270) has two callers: initialise_durable_store (publication.py:320) and _publish_locked (publication.py:813). initialise_durable_store only ever commits the GENESIS watermark (committed_seq=-1, commits nothing; publication.py:235,320) and is called at startup (publisher_service.py:136) and inside _publish_locked (publication.py:731). reconcile_publication_state's ledger write atomic_write_bytes(store.ledger, split.raw[:committed_end_offset]) (publication.py:661) only TRUNCATES a provably-uncommitted tail, gated by _assert_tail_is_provably_uncommitted (publication.py:460,656); it never appends a new anchor nor advances the watermark. mark_anchored (publication.py:642,828; run_identity.py:279) is the RunIdentity state consequence of the commit, explicitly 'never a second authority' (publication.py:22-24,36-39) — not a ledger/watermark writer.

No Anchor V1 writer in production: the writer emits V2 only (CURRENT_ANCHOR_SCHEMA = ANCHOR_SCHEMA_V2, anchor.py:46; build_anchor_record sets schema=CURRENT_ANCHOR_SCHEMA, anchor.py:509). V1 is read-only historical evidence. Both build routes (publish_anchor, durable_publish) go through build_anchor_record (anchor.py:524, publication.py:774), the single record-construction chokepoint (only two callers, grep confirmed).

kernel/authority.py is a pure compatibility RE-EXPORT with NO implementation of its own (authority.py:1-17,20-46) and is imported by NO production module — grep for 'kernel.authority'/'import authority' across src/gnosis returns only docstring mentions (anchor.py:4-5, launch.py:4-5). It is not a live bypass. publish_anchor reached through it is still only called by tests.

No alternate/fallback writers: src/gnosis/director/* has ZERO references to AnchorStore/publish_anchor/durable_publish/watermark/mark_anchored (grep no matches) — no direct Director append; src/gnosis/trust/worker_launcher.py has ZERO anchor/AnchorStore/watermark references (grep no matches) — no same-user launcher fallback; src/gnosis/transport/* has ZERO anchor references — no alternate publisher. AnchorStore is instantiated only in the publisher service (publisher.py:115, publisher_service.py:128), PipeServer only at publisher_service.py:156.

The scripts/ hits (probe_stage6/7/8, mutation_check_*) call AnchorStore/build_anchor_record directly (e.g. probe_stage7_git_matrix.py:241) but are manual verification/mutation harnesses, not wired into the service entry (which is publisher_service.main only) and not reachable from a worker PUBLISH request — test/probe-only, not production-reachable.

finding.details:
Production writes V2 only. There is exactly one method that writes an anchor to disk: AnchorStore.append (anchor.py:263-286). It writes whatever AnchorRecord it is handed. Both production protocols that reach it construct that record through the single shared builder build_anchor_record (anchor.py:450-510), which hardcodes schema=CURRENT_ANCHOR_SCHEMA (line 509), and CURRENT_ANCHOR_SCHEMA = ANCHOR_SCHEMA_V2 = "gnosis.anchor.v2" (lines 46, 37). The builder also sets the two V2-only binding fields (deployment_digest, run_identity_digest) at lines 507-508. The Stage-3 protocol publish_anchor (anchor.py:513-529) and the Stage-4 durable_publish (publication.py:706-777, invoked by the real publisher at publisher.py:201) both call build_anchor_record then store.append — so every production write is V2.

V1 is read/verify-only, historical. The V1 constant is present only in the SUPPORTED (read) set (line 47) and is instantiable only via parse_record_line (line 194), the disk reader used by records()/verify_chain()/lookup()/verify_anchored_bundle(). No production code passes schema=ANCHOR_SCHEMA on a write; the exhaustive greps for AnchorRecord(, store.append, and schema= confirm no second/V1 writer exists. Defence-in-depth in the record itself reinforces the split: __post_init__ (lines 141-149) rejects a V1 record carrying V2 fields and a V2 record missing them (anti-masquerade); to_dict (lines 159-165) emits V2 keys only for V2 so historical V1 digests still re-derive byte-for-byte; and is_deployment_bound (line 176) returns True only for V2, so verify_anchored_bundle refuses to let a V1 record satisfy a bound (F-17) verification (lines 560-563). Note: build_anchor_record additionally gates on a CLEAN boundary verdict (lines 482-488) before producing the V2 record, so the V2 writer is the single F-17 Stage-7 chokepoint. Conclusion: the production writer emits gnosis.anchor.v2 exclusively; V1 is historical read/verify support only. PASS.

verify.reason: Verified against the actual source at C:/Users/nicol/Desktop/Claude Code Proyectos/GnosisAgentAi/src. The anchor record writer is unique and emits V2 only: AnchorRecord(...) is constructed at exactly two sites — anchor.py:501 (build_anchor_record, schema=CURRENT_ANCHOR_SCHEMA hardcoded line 509) and anchor.py:194 (parse_record_line, a reader). CURRENT_ANCHOR_SCHEMA = ANCHOR_SCHEMA_V2 = "gnosis.anchor.v2" (lines 46,37). The only ledger-writing method, AnchorStore.append (opens anchors.jsonl at anchor.py:281), has exactly two production callers, anchor.py:525 (publish_anchor) and publication.py:777 (durable_publish), both fed solely by build_anchor_record. I tried to refute along all five axes and failed: (1) No second production writer — both AnchorStore consumers (publisher.py:115, publisher_service.py:128) route to the same Publisher->durable_publish (publisher.py:201); publisher_service's own store use is startup reconcile/read only; publish_anchor has no wired production caller and would emit V2 anyway. (2) No V1 writer — the V1 constant ANCHOR_SCHEMA appears only in its definition, the SUPPORTED read set, an error string, and the static re-export kernel/authority.py (which has no implementation). (3) Fault seam not worker-reachable — _FAULT_HOOK defaults None (publication.py:139), never assigned anywhere in src. (4) No closure leak — schema is a module constant applied at the call site. (5) No dynamic import/exec/eval in anchor.py. The only other ledger mutation, publication.py:661 atomic_write_bytes, writes back only the already-committed prefix bytes during tail discard (constructs no record, emits no schema), consistent with V1 being historical/read-only. Reinforcing controls verified: publisher.py:188 refuses non-V2 identities, plus __post_init__ anti-masquerade (137-149), to_dict V2-key-only (159-165), is_deployment_bound V2-only (176), verify_anchored_bundle refusing V1 for bound checks (560-563), and the CLEAN boundary-verdict gate (482-488). All cited line numbers match. No counterexample found.

finding.claim: The Stage 4 durable-publication fault-injection seam is settable only by trusted (non-worker) in-process code; no worker-controlled input (IPC request string, LaunchSpec fields, candidate evidence bytes, worker environment, or run_id) can activate it.
evidence: The seam has two surfaces that reduce to ONE root. (1) publication._FAULT_HOOK: module-private global defined `_FAULT_HOOK: Any = None` at src/gnosis/trust/publication.py:139; fired via `_fault(point, **context)` at publication.py:142-145, which calls the hook ONLY `if hook is not None` (hook = _FAULT_HOOK). (2) anchor.AnchorStore.append(record, *, fault=None) at src/gnosis/trust/anchor.py:263, fired via `_fire(fault, point, ...)` at anchor.py:87-89 only `if fault is not None`.

The anchor seam is fed exclusively by the same global. Only production caller passing fault= is src/gnosis/trust/publication.py:777 `store.append(record, fault=_FAULT_HOOK)`. The only other append() with a possible fault in src is the Stage-3 path src/gnosis/trust/anchor.py:525 `store.append(record)` which passes nothing (-> None). Grep of `.append(` across src/gnosis/trust confirms no other fault-bearing caller.

Every way to SET the seam is trusted-only. The sole assignments to _FAULT_HOOK anywhere in the tree are the `= None` default at publication.py:139 and test files under tests/ (test_durable_publication.py:651,677,959,1071; test_publisher_service.py). No src module other than publication.py assigns it (grep `_FAULT_HOOK\s*=` in src returns only publication.py:139 def + :777 read). AST guard tests/test_publisher_service.py:490-499 (test_only_the_publication_module_assigns_the_hook) enforces this and passes.

Channel 1 (IPC request string): the ENTIRE request grammar is `_REQUEST = re.compile(r"^PUBLISH (?P<run_id>[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9._-]{0,127})$")` at src/gnosis/trust/publisher.py:59. Anchored ^...$, one verb, one run_id token; any other shape -> `_refused("bad-request")` at publisher.py:158-162. There is no --fault / key=value / hook parse. Captured run_id flows to durable_publish(store, run_store, request, bundle_dir, *, verify, repair_uncommitted_tail) at publication.py:706 — signature has NO fault parameter, nor does _publish_locked (publication.py:724). Runtime-proven: tests/test_publisher_service.py:460-470 (test_no_request_installs_a_fault_hook) feeds `PUBLISH F5`, `PUBLISH run-1 --fault=F5`, `_FAULT_HOOK F5`, `FAULT F5`, etc. and asserts publication._FAULT_HOOK stays None — PASSED.

Channel 2 (worker-facing LaunchSpec fields): identity.launch_spec_digest/epoch/repository_id/head_sha/tree_identity come from the TRUSTED run store (record.identity at publisher.py:163-167) and are used only as expected_* comparison fields in PublicationRequest (publisher.py:131-153). None is a fault selector and durable_publish exposes no fault parameter, so a LaunchSpec digest is compared, never routed to _FAULT_HOOK.

Channel 3 (candidate evidence bytes): bundle bytes are consumed by build_anchor_record(store, identity, bundle_dir, verify) at publication.py:774 and verify_bundle to compute bundle_digest; no code path assigns _FAULT_HOOK from bundle content. The _fault/_fire firing decision is `hook/fault is not None` (publication.py:144, anchor.py:88), independent of any evidence byte.

Channel 4 (worker environment): publication.py and anchor.py contain no environ/getenv/argv/argparse/input/stdin reads (only the words appear in comments). AST-proven by tests/test_publisher_service.py:471-479 (test_the_seam_reads_no_environment_and_no_configuration) and tests/test_durable_publication.py:1289-1304 (test_no_environment_or_argument_can_switch_a_fault_on) — both PASSED. Service configuration itself comes only from an admin-provisioned JSON file named on the service command line, never from the wire (src/gnosis/trust/publisher_service.py:12-20 docstring, ServiceConfig.load at :64-95), and _REQUIRED (:44-48) contains no fault field.

Channel 5 (run_id): run_id is a pure selector (publisher.py:163 `run_id = match.group('run_id')`), flows into durable_publish (no fault param) and appears in _fault(...)/_fire(...) calls only as forwarded **context (publication.py:773, 826, 827, 833; anchor.py:282, 284). Context is passed to an ALREADY-installed hook; it never decides whether the hook fires — the `is not None` gate does. So no worker-derived context value (run_id, identity, record) can activate the seam.

Clean-interpreter default is None: runtime-proven by tests/test_durable_publication.py:1280-1287 (test_the_hook_is_none_in_a_clean_interpreter) which imports publication in a fresh subprocess and prints None — PASSED. The seam is inert with no hook installed (test_the_seam_is_inert_with_no_hook_installed, :1307-1311).

Runtime confirmation: `.venv/Scripts/python -m unittest tests.test_publisher_service` -> all guard tests OK (including test_no_request_installs_a_fault_hook, test_only_the_publication_module_assigns_the_hook, test_the_seam_reads_no_environment_and_no_configuration); `-m unittest tests.test_durable_publication.TestTheFaultSeamIsNotReachableFromAnyInput` -> Ran 4 tests, OK.
finding.details:
Files: C:/Users/nicol/Desktop/Claude Code Proyectos/GnosisAgentAi/src/gnosis/trust/publication.py, /anchor.py, /publisher.py, /publisher_service.py; guards in tests/test_publisher_service.py and tests/test_durable_publication.py.

Reduction: The seam is a single root — the module-private global publication._FAULT_HOOK (publication.py:139), which defaults to None. Both firing sites are None-gated: _fault fires only `if hook is not None` (publication.py:144) and _fire only `if fault is not None` (anchor.py:88). anchor.AnchorStore.append's `fault` keyword-only parameter (anchor.py:263) is the second surface, but its only production caller is publication.py:777 `store.append(record, fault=_FAULT_HOOK)`, so it is driven entirely by the same global; the Stage-3 caller anchor.py:525 omits it. Therefore proving the seam safe reduces to proving _FAULT_HOOK is set only by trusted code and that append() has no other fault-passing caller — both confirmed.

Set-paths: The only assignments to _FAULT_HOOK are the `= None` default and test-suite assignments; no src module besides publication.py assigns it (AST-enforced by test_only_the_publication_module_assigns_the_hook, which handles AnnAssign specifically). durable_publish/_publish_locked, the public entrypoints reachable from IPC, have no fault parameter.

Worker channels, each blocked: (1) IPC string — grammar `^PUBLISH <run_id>$` (publisher.py:59) admits only one selector token; anything else is refused; no fault parse exists; durable_publish has no fault arg. (2) LaunchSpec fields — arrive from the trusted store as comparison-only expected_* values. (3) evidence bytes — only hashed into a digest; firing is content-independent. (4) environment — no environ/getenv/argv/argparse/stdin anywhere in the two modules (AST-proven), and service config is an admin JSON file, never the wire. (5) run_id — a selector that, at most, is forwarded as **context to an already-installed trusted hook; context never gates firing.

Trusted test code setting it directly (e.g. tests/test_durable_publication.py:650-655) is the accepted, permitted mechanism.

Verification: ran the dedicated guard suites under the project venv (Python 3.13); all passed, including a fresh-subprocess check that the hook imports as None and AST checks that no worker-influenceable input can install one. Verdict: PASS — the seam is settable only by trusted, in-process (TCB) code.
